## Body

Lessons from #130, #138 and #144 on 06 Nov (pij-local-warbler, lanes C and plan 209).

1. Check live state before acting on "merge main / push". pm-001's queued sends arrived 4 to 9 hours late and out of order (F69). Six asks to merge #130 came after it had already merged. Run `gh pr view N --json state,headRefOid,mergeable` first, and answer with the head and state.

2. When two branches both append tests at the end of a file, git's conflict hunks interleave on identical lines (`], &repo.main, ).await;`). Keeping "ours then theirs" per hunk splits a test across blocks. Rebuild the region instead: ours = hunk1-ours + common + hunk2-ours + ..., then theirs the same way, and emit ours, then theirs. Then grep for duplicated `mod x;` lines and run rustfmt, which catches broken delimiters.

3. A merge can need behaviour, not just text. When two features meet, check each hook still fires on every path: 208's `assign --batch` returned before 202's routes FYI, so batch holders never got the table. Say any such addition in the merge commit.

4. Held FYIs ride along with a seat's next real message. A test that compares a delivered body exactly breaks once another feature holds an FYI for that seat (#129's drain test after #130). Compare the request part and allow only the known rider.

5. Background QoS (`taskpolicy -b`) makes timing tests fail; a full daemon-lib run failed 1 to 17 of 758 at load 25 to 49. Compile with `cargo test --no-run` under `nice -n 19 taskpolicy -b`, then run the copied binaries under `nice -n 19` alone. shared-build does this itself after #144 (F63).

6. Before trusting a loop that "fails every run", check the filter matched: `--exact` with a wrong module path ran 0 tests. Grep the log for " 1 passed".
